title: Opt-in native conformance evidence for COMP-KERNEL and COMP-FIXTURES
summary: Compliance C31. @inventarch/compliance adds verifyKernel(floor?) and verifyFixtures(), isConformanceEvidence(value, subject?), CONFORMANCE_PROFILE ('package-v1') and the KernelEvidence, FixtureEvidence, ConformanceEvidence, ConformanceToolchain, ConformanceProfile, OutOfProfileSuite, KernelSource, ConformanceOptions and ConformanceSummary types. verifyKernel regenerates the kernel from a floor (the embedded one by default) in-process and compares it with the running @inventarch/language; verifyFixtures runs the package-v1 profile of the shipped language, refusal and evidence fixtures against a generated inventory. Both run only when called and read only this package's own files. Their evidence is deeply frozen and accepted only from the producing module instance. evaluate's new opt-in conformance: {inputs, kernel, fixtures} option binds that evidence to the evaluated graph: evidence for another revision, language version, kernel digest, floor or toolchain stays not-evaluated, each check judged on its own evidence, a verified failure on the graph's own floor fails, and copied, hand-built or swapped evidence, or evidence together with conformance, is a TypeError. evaluate reads the inputs once and refuses fields that are not strings. Results verified from evaluated evidence carry the new Verdict.basis 'verified' and add Report.conformance for those checks, a verified fixture result with the suites it did not run. Results taken from the caller-asserted evidence map now carry basis 'caller-asserted' and are rebuilt from their check, scope, outcome and findings, so other keys a caller put on such a verdict no longer reach the report: outcomes are unchanged, but reports from callers that pass the map change digest. Reports that pass neither option are unchanged. Limits: the profile does not run the hook, runtime, execution or publication suites, and every fixture result lists them as out of profile; the evidence verifies the installed package against itself, and the binding trusts the Graph it is given, so a consumer pins kernelDigest and inventoryDigest and relies on npm integrity.
